findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 3 projects, synced last week." is followed by a list containing only "Data Warehouse Cutover" and "Mobile App Revamp"
findings.fix: List all 3 projects, or relabel the list as "Recent projects" and add a link to a full project list that accounts for the third one.
findings.location: Workspace overview section, "Your projects" heading, the recent projects list under id="workspace-overview-recent"
findings.violation: The stated project count is 3 but only 2 projects appear anywhere in the document, so a user counting what they see cannot reconcile the number with the list.

findings.evidence: "Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on."
findings.fix: Make the banner a link or button that goes directly to the invite flow (id="invite-member"), or remove it if it is not meant to be actionable here.
findings.location: Workspace overview section, promo banner with id="workspace-overview-promo-referral"
findings.violation: This call to action is plain text with no link or button, so a user who wants to act on it has no way to do so from this screen.

findings.evidence: The form wrapping the name input and the Save button has no action or method attribute
findings.fix: Give the form an explicit action or intercept the submit and show a confirmation state, consistent with how the rest of the document handles transitions.
findings.location: Project settings section, the project name form
findings.violation: Submitting this form has no defined destination, so clicking Save will attempt to reload the current page instead of confirming the save within this document's anchor based flow.

findings.fix: Add visible label text such as "Duplicate project" (or an aria-label if an icon-only design is intentional).
findings.location: Project settings section, the button with id="project-settings-duplicate-btn"
findings.violation: The button has no visible text and no aria-label, so neither a sighted user nor a screen reader user can tell what pressing it will do.

findings.evidence: The form's submit button is labeled "Save" and a separate link, id="invite-member-continue-link", labeled "Continue," both appear to lead toward completing the invite
findings.fix: Reduce this to one clearly labeled action such as "Send invite," or explain in the interface what each control does if they are genuinely separate steps.
findings.violation: It is not clear whether "Save" or "Continue" is the action that actually sends the invite, or whether both are required, so a user can leave the screen unsure if the invite was sent.

findings.evidence: The section contains only a heading and the paragraph "An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted." with no link or button anywhere in it
findings.fix: Add a link back to project settings or the workspace overview, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the document.
findings.violation: This screen is a dead end. Every other section in the document provides at least one way to navigate onward, but this one gives the user no way back to their project or workspace.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list."
findings.fix: Either build an archived projects view and link to it from the workspace overview, or remove the restore claim from this copy.
findings.location: Archive confirmation section, paragraph with id="archive-confirm-copy"
findings.violation: No "archived projects list" page or link exists anywhere in this document, so this promise cannot actually be fulfilled by the user.

findings.evidence: The head contains only a charset meta tag and the title "Project workspace mockup," no viewport meta tag
findings.fix: Add a viewport meta tag, for example <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">, to the head.
findings.violation: Without a viewport meta tag, this page will not scale correctly on mobile browser widths, which undermines usability on any device narrower than a desktop.

findings.fix: Add a name attribute, for example name="digest-frequency", to the select element.
findings.location: Notification settings section, the digest frequency field with id="notification-settings-digest-input"
findings.violation: Even if this form were wired up to submit, the selected digest frequency would never actually be sent because the field has no name attribute, so a user's choice could not be saved.
